in_latin.name: Burgess
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Burgess originates from the Latin 'burgus', meaning 'town' or 'fortress'. In medieval Europe, a burgess was a freeman who lived in a town or city and enjoyed certain rights and privileges. The name reflects the social status of a person who was part of the emerging middle class in urban centers.
